statement_nl: Let $f\\colon [0,1] \\to [0, \\infty)$ be strictly increasing and continuous. Let $R$ be the region bounded by $x=0$, $x=1$, $y=0$, and $y=f(x)$. Let $x_1$ be the $x$-coordinate of the centroid of $R$. Let $x_2$ be the $x$-coordinate of the centroid of the solid generated by rotating $R$ around the $x$-axis. Prove that $x_1 < x_2$.

domain_restrictions: f is continuous on [0,1] and strictly increasing (hence measurable and integrable).
f is not identically zero (strictly increasing prevents f constant), so ∫_0^1 f(x) dx > 0 and ∫_0^1 f(x)^2 dx > 0 (denominators in centroid formulas are nonzero).
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For every continuous strictly increasing f:[0,1]→[0,∞) with ∫_0^1 f > 0 and ∫_0^1 f^2 > 0, define x1 = (∫_0^1 x f)/(∫_0^1 f) and x2 = (∫_0^1 x f^2)/(∫_0^1 f^2). Then x2 - x1 = (1/(2 ∫ f ∫ f^2)) ∫_0^1∫_0^1 (x-y)(f(x)-f(y)) f(x) f(y) dx dy > 0, hence x1 < x2.
quantifier_order: For all functions f: [0,1] → [0,∞) that are continuous and strictly increasing, define R from f and define x1 and x2 as below; then claim x1 < x2.

variables.name: f
variables.role: given integrable height function, continuous and strictly increasing, with range in [0,∞)

variables.name: R
variables.role: plane lamina region whose centroid's x-coordinate is x1

variables.name: x1
variables.role: x-coordinate of planar centroid (lamina) for uniform density

variables.domain: x-coordinate of centroid of the solid of revolution of R about the x-axis
variables.name: x2
variables.role: x-coordinate of centroid of 3D solid (uniform density)

witness_dependencies: x1 depends on f via the formula x1 = (∫_0^1 x f(x) dx) / (∫_0^1 f(x) dx).
x2 depends on f via the formula x2 = (∫_0^1 x f(x)^2 dx) / (∫_0^1 f(x)^2 dx) (π cancels from numerator and denominator of the centroid formula for solid of revolution).
The difference x2 - x1 is equal to ((∫ x f^2)(∫ f) - (∫ x f)(∫ f^2)) / (∫ f^2 ∫ f), so sign is determined by the numerator, which depends solely on f.
